subject: maths
question: Two trains running in opposite direction on parallel tracks, at the speed of 48 km/h and 52 km/h, take 27 seconds to cross each other. If the lenght of one train is 350 m then find the length ( in metres) of the other train?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (opposite direction) = 48 + 52 = 100 km/h = 100 × 5/18 = 250/9 m/s.

Total distance (Sum of lengths) = Speed × Time = (250/9) × 27 = 750 m.

Length of the other train = Total distance − First train length = 750 − 350 = 400 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 400 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the first train (S₁) = 48 km/h

Speed of the second train (S₂) = 52 km/h

Time taken to cross each other (T) = 27 seconds

Length of the first train (L₁) = 350 m

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (when moving in opposite directions) = S₁ + S₂

Total Distance (L₁ + L₂) = Relative Speed × Time

 
 Train 1 : 48 km/h
 Length = 350 m
 
 
• 
 

 

 
 Train 2 : 52 km/h
 Length = ?
 
 
• 
 

 

 27 sec
 

 

 
 Relative Speed = 48 + 52 = 100 km/h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 48 + 52 = 100 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 100 × 5/18 = 250/9 m/s

⇒ Total Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Total Distance = (250/9) × 27

⇒ Total Distance = 250 × 3 = 750 m

⇒ L₁ + L₂ = 750

⇒ 350 + L₂ = 750

⇒ L₂ = 750 − 350 = 400 m

**∴ The correct answer is 400 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds. Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|.

Conversion of Speed Units

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing a Stationary Object

When a train crosses a stationary pole or man, the total distance covered is exactly equal to the length of the train.

Crossing a Bridge or Platform

When a train crosses a stationary bridge or platform, the total distance covered is the sum of the length of the train and the length of the bridge/platform.
